statusText: Tail rises to 20%. Mapped policy state: WATCH. The upside retracement flagged in the prior hour has failed: after basing at 30,918.77, cash NDX rallied to 31,125.13 and has since given the move back, trading 30,986.03, -0.56%. NQ Dec26 holds 31,237.00, -0.53%, and its 31,120.00 session low is still intact after roughly three hours. That combination is two-sided rotation rather than persistent one-way structure, which is why Tail moves only one point above the watch boundary instead of approaching the blocking threshold. Stress stays high at 65% because WTI is +5.17% at $92.84 and Brent +5.26% at $105.48 on Gulf shipping attacks and storm-related production shut-ins, the long end sits near multidecade highs at 10Y 5.31% and 30Y 5.67%, and the Russell 2000 is materially weaker than the Nasdaq. Against that, VIX at 15.46 remains well below its 16.02 session high, so the volatility market is not confirming the cross-asset stress.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is WATCH with Tail at 20%, one point inside the 20-24% watch band and well below the 25% blocking threshold. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 17:00Z-19:00Z, spanning the 30-year bond auction and the Fed Musalem speech, where conditional Tail ridges to 23%. No slot in the 24-hour published path reaches the blocking threshold. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 gives back its intraday bounce but holds the session low as a 5% oil shock meets a 15.5 VIX, lifting Tail one point into the watch band ahead of the 30-year auction
body:
The Nasdaq-100 is trading two-sided inside a session range rather than trending. Cash NDX set its 30,918.77 low early in the U.S. session, recovered to 31,125.13, and has since rolled back to 30,986.03, -174.04 or -0.56% against the 31,160.08 prior close. NQ Dec26 is 31,237.00, -165.25 or -0.53%, inside a 31,120.00-31,466.00 range whose low has now held for approximately three hours. The failed upside retracement is the one genuinely Tail-relevant development of the hour, because it establishes that the bounce lacked follow-through; the offsetting fact is that the downside low has not been extended either. Neither side of the range is producing the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure that defines a pathological price path, so Tail stays near the watch boundary at 20% rather than moving toward the 25% block.

The stress backdrop is genuinely difficult. Crude is the day's dominant macro impulse, with WTI +5.17% at $92.84 and Brent +5.26% at $105.48, attributed in current reporting to renewed attacks on Gulf and Strait of Hormuz shipping, reports that further U.S. strikes on Iran are under consideration, and Gulf of Mexico production shut-ins ahead of a tropical storm. That oil move feeds directly into the inflation channel at a moment when the long end is already near multidecade highs: the 10-year is 5.31% and the 30-year 5.67%, with the 2-year up roughly six basis points to 4.83% after initial jobless claims fell to 197,000 against a 200,000 consensus. Breadth confirms the rate sensitivity, with the Russell 2000 down materially more than the Nasdaq and Intel off more than 3%.

The decisive counter-evidence is the volatility market. VIX at 15.46 is up only 2.52% and sits far below its 16.02 session high, which is not the profile of an index pricing a disorderly path. Under the governing contract, event importance, a large oil move and cross-asset stress primarily raise Stress and inform Confidence; they do not mechanically raise Tail without observed mean-reversion failure. Stress is therefore carried at 65% while Tail stays at 20%.

The forward path concentrates conditional risk in a narrow 17:00Z-19:00Z window containing the 30-year bond auction and the Fed Musalem speech. With the 30-year at 5.67%, a weak auction is the most credible mechanism for aligning yields, breadth and the index into the sustained pressure that Tail actually measures, including the delayed second leg in which the bond reaction arrives before the equity response. Conditional Tail peaks at 23% in that window, decays to an 11% trough across the Asian hours, and rebuilds to 21% by Friday's 14:00Z Michigan preliminary release, whose inflation-expectations components carry extra weight while crude is 5% higher. No published slot reaches the blocking threshold.

Shared Finviz context was read at the start of this run and deliberately not used: its payload carries a 2026-09-29 collection timestamp and a partial collection status, which is far outside the 90-minute freshness limit the provider contract sets for supporting use. The assessment rests entirely on independently fetched primary sources, and evidence availability is otherwise good, supporting Confidence at 88%.

lookbackSummary: The 24 hours to 14:00Z cover a full decay-and-rebuild cycle. Tail entered the window at 20% during Wednesday's U.S. afternoon, fell steadily to a 10% trough by 03:00Z as the overnight session mean-reverted cleanly, then rebuilt sharply from 06:00Z as the oil impulse and the long-end yield move reasserted themselves into the European morning, peaking at 23% in the 11:00Z hour. Stress climbed monotonically across almost the whole window, from 52% to a 66% peak, which is the signature of a worsening environment rather than a failing price path. The final two slots show the divergence clearly: the 13:00Z hour published 21% and the 14:00Z hour 17% as the U.S. cash open was absorbed without downside continuation. Every one of the 24 slots is an actual published Claude assessment; none is reconstructed, and no past opinion has been revised with hindsight.
outlookSummary: Conditional Tail stays inside the watch band or lower for all 24 slots and never approaches the 25% blocking threshold. It holds at 20-21% through the remainder of the U.S. cash session, ridges to a 23% window peak in the 17:00Z hour containing the 30-year bond auction and the Fed Musalem speech, eases to 22% during auction digestion at 18:00Z, then decays through the 20:00Z cash close to an 11% trough across the 03:00Z-04:00Z Asia-to-Europe handover. The narrow 17:00Z-19:00Z danger window covers only the two highest slots. From 05:00Z the path climbs gradually to 20% at Friday's 13:00Z U.S. cash open and 21% in the 14:00Z hour containing the Michigan preliminary release. Confidence decays from 88% to 75% across the window as the basis shifts from observed structure to assumption.
